description: The link between Rack and a Haken Eagan Matrix instrument: it holds the MIDI connection, scans the presets, and carries the surface out as control voltage; other CHEM modules work through one

params.text: Passes only notes and expression from that controller to the instrument, dropping the control messages that would otherwise change the preset
Blocks everything from that controller, which mutes it without unplugging it
Counts up one per second to a maximum of 60 minutes and then wraps to zero; nothing in the module or in the instrument reads it
Reflects music on MIDI channels 2 and up from that controller down to channels 15 and below, so a second Eagan Matrix surface can be played at the same time without note collisions
Sets the master level on the instrument, which is attenuation on Haken instruments and post level on an Osmose
Slews the Y output, with no slew fully anticlockwise and the slowest movement fully clockwise
Slews the Z output, with no slew fully anticlockwise and the slowest movement fully clockwise
Lengthens the slew range of the two trim pots beside the Y and Z outputs by a factor of ten
Sends a short test phrase of MIDI notes to the instrument, so you can hear whether the connection carries sound

inputs.text: A high gate blocks that controller's MIDI from reaching the instrument and lights the button beside it; the gate reads high at 0.8V and above

outputs.text: Carries 10V while the instrument is able to accept MIDI and make sound, and 0V while it is busy loading a preset, scanning presets or remaking Mahling data
Carries 10V on a channel while a note is held on that channel of the playing surface, and 0V when the note ends
The pitch of the note held on that channel, as a volt per octave with the surface's pitch bend folded in; 0V is MIDI note 60
The front-to-back position on that channel, 0-10V, taken from whichever continuous controller the instrument has assigned to Y
The pressure on that channel, 0-10V, taken from whichever continuous controller the instrument has assigned to Z

notes: a module added to a patch finds the first Eagan Matrix instrument connected to the computer and connects to it; if there is more than one, click the HAKEN button to choose
MIDI usually stays silent unless the patch also holds one of the VCV Audio modules with a driver chosen, so add an Audio module before this one
the Preset and Play modules show nothing until the presets have been scanned into a database, which is started from the Presets submenu of the Core actions menu on this panel
the C1 and c2 buttons choose MIDI controllers whose data is passed on to the instrument; the MIDI Reset button above HAKEN restarts the connection, and control-clicking it clears every one
to control a second Eagan Matrix instrument, add a second one of these to the patch
menu: Presets — on the Core actions menu reached from the hamburger button, not the right-click menu; scans the instrument to build the preset databases Preset and Play read
Log MIDI — on the Core actions menu; writes every MIDI message sent and received into a log file in the pachde-CHEM folder under your Rack user folder
Disconnect MIDI — on the Core actions menu; drops the MIDI connection to the instrument until it is turned off again
Zero XYZ on Note off — on the Core actions menu; drops the X, Y and Z voltage for a channel to zero when the note ends, in place of holding the last value
MPE channels (2-15) only — on the Core actions menu; makes the W, X, Y and Z outputs 14 channels taken from MIDI channels 2 to 15, in place of 16 channels taken from every MIDI channel
Silence WYXZ — on the Core actions menu; clears the stored note, bend, front-to-back and pressure for every channel, so the four surface outputs fall to 0V
Haken Requests — on the Core actions menu; sends single requests from the Haken MIDI protocol to the instrument, for working out what has gone wrong
